overall_notes: The engineering scaffolding is unusually thorough: gates, lifecycle classifier, hard-stop concerns, backups, CI, an honest session log, and a working save/share/calendar/tickets layer. What the site actually shows lags behind it. The biggest risks are to correctness and to citability. (1) About 51 athinorama year-rollover phantom events (12% of the 429 listed) appear as future events, rank first in search, and publish false startDates in JSON-LD. (2) Megaron rows carry a source-wide default of 20:30 / €25, which I proved wrong against megaron.gr for tours and family events. (3) Template leakage is visible to users: the '<!-- timeliness-expires -->' comment on 686 pages and in JSON-LD, and '[PLACEHOLDER]' copy on 6 hubs. Coverage is thin (4 exhibitions, 3 cinema listings, 5 events 'tonight'). The Greek locale has no Greek descriptions, and its hubs are noindexed with no hreflang anywhere. Measurement, INTENT's focus #1, is essentially empty: citations and crawlers are null, and GA4 AI referrals have been stale since June. Scores reflect the local build (ahead of live). The live site was checked only for freshness, headers, compressed size and LCP.
